title: Proposed Constitutional Amendment: To Require Voters to Present Photo Identification in Order to Vote
plain_english: This amendment would put Ohio's voter photo-ID requirement in the state constitution. Ohio law already requires photo ID for in-person voting. If approved, the amendment would set the accepted ID list in the constitution, allow an alternative identity check for voters with a sincere religious objection to being photographed, and add identity rules for voters using other voting methods. It would take effect immediately. Changing the constitutional requirement would require another statewide vote.
yes_means: The amendment takes effect immediately and adds an approved government-issued photo-ID requirement to the Ohio Constitution. The listed IDs are an unexpired Ohio driver license or state ID, a U.S. passport or passport card, a U.S. military ID, an Ohio National Guard ID, or a U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs ID. State law may provide another identity-verification method for an in-person voter with a sincere religious objection to being photographed. Voters who do not vote in person must provide an approved photo ID unless Ohio law authorizes a signature plus at least one other specified unique identifier.
no_means: The Constitution stays unchanged. Ohio's current photo-ID law for in-person voting remains in place, but this amendment does not add its photo-ID rules to the Constitution. The General Assembly remains able to change statutory voting rules through legislation.
official_ballot_language: Proposed Constitutional Amendment. Proposed by Joint Resolution of the General Assembly. To enact Section 5 of Article V of the Constitution of the State of Ohio. A majority yes vote is required for the adoption of Section 5. This proposed amendment would: • Require voters to present an approved form of government-issued photo identification in order to vote. • Allow state law to provide for an alternative method of verifying a voter’s identity for a voter who has a sincere religious objection to being photographed and, therefore, does not possess an approved form of government-issued photo identification. • Require that voters who do not vote in person provide an approved form of government-issued photo identification, unless the law authorizes those persons to vote by providing a signature and at least one other specified unique identifier. • Define approved forms of government-issued photo identification as an unexpired Ohio driver license or state identification card; a United States passport or passport card; or a United States military identification card, Ohio National Guard identification card, or United States Department of Veterans Affairs identification card. If approved, the amendment shall take effect immediately. A “YES” vote means approval of the amendment. A “NO” vote means disapproval of the amendment. YES. SHALL THE AMENDMENT BE APPROVED? NO. TO REQUIRE VOTERS TO PRESENT PHOTO IDENTIFICATION IN ORDER TO VOTE.
supporters_say: The official pro-amendment argument (authors: State Reps. Adam Bird and Heidi Workman, State Sens. Theresa Gavarone and Jane Timken) says: 'Requiring a photo ID helps verify a voter's identity and ensures that only legal votes are counted,' calling it a 'commonsense requirement' that 'will protect Ohio's elections.'
opponents_say: The official anti-amendment argument (authors: State Sen. Bill DeMora, State Reps. Desiree Tims and Terrence Upchurch) calls it a 'blatant political attack' on citizens' right to vote, arguing 'Photo Identification is already the law and this amendment locks in voter burden with no voter protections' and 'Voter impersonation is essentially nonexistent.'

title: Proposed Charter Amendment - City of Conneaut (Ban on Large Data Centers)
plain_english: This would amend Conneaut's city charter to prohibit construction of a data center. The definition covers one or more buildings, facilities, or infrastructure (including equipment cooling systems) primarily or exclusively used for digital information services when their combined monthly demand or peak load is more than 25 megawatts. Facilities on a single parcel, or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated parcels, can count together; the threshold can be reached using any energy source or a combination. The charter defines construction to include related preparation and modification work.
yes_means: The charter would prohibit construction of any data center meeting the measure's definition, including facilities on one parcel or aggregated parcels whose combined monthly demand or peak load exceeds 25 megawatts. The ban would include related preparation and modification work and would take effect on its own, without further city action.
no_means: The charter would remain unchanged, and this measure would not create the proposed data-center construction ban.
official_ballot_language: A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall the Charter of the City of Conneaut be amended to add Article XVI to read as follows: ARTICLE XVI CONSERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES. Section XVI-1. Prohibition of Construction of a Data Center. (A) The construction of a data center is hereby prohibited. (B) As used in this Section, “construction” shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities, and related activities, which include preparations and modifications for same, for a common purpose. (C) As used in this Section, “data center” shall mean one or more buildings or physical facilities or infrastructure, located on a single real property parcel or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels that (1) Are used primarily or exclusively for digital information services such as the management, storage, processing, and dissemination of electronic data and information through the use of computer systems, servers, networking equipment, and related components, including equipment cooling systems; and (2) Has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of greater than twenty five (25) megawatts, however derived from any energy source, or a combination thereof. (D) This Section is self-executing. Shall the proposed charter amendment be adopted? YES / NO.
supporters_say: The petition drive was organized locally with support from the group Conserve Ohio. Petition signature collector Joel Specht said of the rumored project: 'We know there has been one in the works.' Organic farmer Julia Barton cited heavy water use and excessive noise, saying the development 'has the potential to be a detriment to the things that sustain us.'
opponents_say: UNVERIFIED - no published statements from local opponents of the Conneaut ban were found in available sources.
context: Developer M2 Development Solutions has been studying a data center at the Conneaut East Industrial Park, and the city council rejected a proposed data-center moratorium in 2026. Nine Ohio communities have matching 25-megawatt ban petitions, and 18 Ohio communities total are voting on data-center measures Nov. 3.
